reason: Conversation 2 reached the correct diagnosis efficiently: failed fan element, confirmed by the customer's visual inspection after isolating. It then answered the model-number question and gave a confirmed-fit element at £30, with an engineer as the fallback. That matches the expected direction. Conversation 1 had better early diagnostics (manual-mode check, thermostat light, isolation steps), but it over-escalated at the end. It told the customer to get an engineer, not to use the grill, and implied the element had 'shorted' and scorched the wiring, none of which the facts support. It also gave no part guidance, even though a swap by a competent DIYer is acceptable. Conversation 2 is weakened by the '[object Object]' glitch and by giving no safety reminder to isolate before fitting.
